title: [finding] the #9137 freeze note in security-plugin.ts cites record-validator.ts:993/:1003 for the provenance skip — both rotted, the guard is at :1037/:1047
body:
Found while implementing #13722 (the adjacent paragraph in the same file). Filed unassigned and out of scope for #13722, whose ruling scopes it to the one `[#8959]` paragraph and explicitly fences the rest of the file. **Recording only, no severity asserted** — routing is triage's.

Same class as #13556 (rotted line anchors into `sql-driver.ts`), but a different carrier and a different site: there the anchor lives in an **ADR** and points into `sql-driver.ts`; here it lives in a **governed source comment** — the ADR-0055 / #9137 FREEZE NOTE — and points into `record-validator.ts`. #13556's scope table does not reach it.

## Measured on `origin/main` at `b8c4762c7`

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:6533` (inside the `[#9137]` freeze note in `assertControlledByParentWrite`) reads, verbatim:

> ... and exactly the three shapes `record-validator.ts` skips before its
> required check ever runs (`if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;`,
> insert-mode :993 / update-mode :1003)

Both anchors have rotted:

| anchor | what the freeze note says is there | what is actually at that line |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `record-validator.ts:993` | `if (def.system \|\| def.readonly) continue;` (insert mode) | `* behavior for any caller that has no principal to read a locale from.` — prose inside an unrelated docblock |
| `record-validator.ts:1003` | the same guard, update mode | a bare `*` continuation line in that same docblock |

The guard it names is really at **`:1037`** (insert) and **`:1047`** (update):

```
$ grep -n "if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;" packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts
1037:      if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;
1047:      if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;
```

Control that the zero above is a reading and not a broken path: the file resolves and is **1073** lines (`wc -l`), so `:993` and `:1003` are both **in range** — they resolve to real lines that say something else. That is the failure mode #13556 names: an anchor that is out of range announces itself, an anchor that lands on unrelated code does not.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

The carrier is not ordinary prose. It is the **freeze note** — the block that tells the next author "do NOT widen `omissionRefusedByValidation` for these three shapes", and whose whole authority rests on the reader being able to go check that `record-validator.ts` really does skip them. A reader who follows the two anchors lands on locale-default prose, finds no guard, and has to decide whether the freeze note is describing code that no longer exists. The anchors are the freeze note's only evidence pointer.

Same reasoning as #13556: a rotted anchor does not fail loudly, and it costs the reader more than a missing one would.

## Suggested fix

Comments-only, one line: replace `:993 / :1003` with a **symbol-relative** citation rather than fresh line numbers, so it cannot rot the same way again — e.g. name the two loop bodies (`validateRecord` insert branch / update branch) instead of positions. #13788 is queueing exactly that treatment (line citations to symbol anchors) for the platform checklist; the same argument applies here. If a positional citation is kept anyway, the current values are `:1037` and `:1047`.

## Not touched here

#13722 is graded `Clause-②: no` and scoped by its claim comment to the one `[#8959]` paragraph, with the rest of `security-plugin.ts` explicitly out of scope. Folding this in would have widened a fenced card, so it is filed instead.
